It becomes spatially non-uniform and can contain competing exchange pathways, weakening coherent interlayer magnetic order while preserving robust intralayer ferromagnetic correlations.
This indicates that exchange inhomogeneity provides an additional mechanism for reducing the thermal stability of the bulk magnetic state.

entities.name: TC reduction in the mixed-orbital/compositional system is not explained by anisotropy averaging alone. Coexistence of distinct local orbital environments and anisotropies perturbs the interlayer V-I..
entities.description: TC reduction in the mixed-orbital/compositional system is not explained by anisotropy averaging alone. Coexistence of distinct local orbital environments and anisotropies perturbs the interlayer V-I...I-V super-superexchange geometry, making like-site and mixed-site interlayer exchange paths differ in strength and even sign. This creates a spatially non-uniform, frustrated interlayer exchange network with competing pathways; the resulting exchange inhomogeneity weakens coherent interlayer magnetic order while preserving strong intralayer ferromagnetic correlations, providing an additional mechanism that suppresses bulk thermal stability and lowers TC.
entities.evidence_span: These results show that the reduction of TC with decreasing CHO is not controlled by anisotropy averaging alone. The smaller anisotropy of LO sites weakens the local stabilization of the ordered moments, whereas the environment-dependent exchange modifies the connectivity of the HO–HO, LO–LO, and HO–LO exchange paths. As a result, the effective magnetic coupling becomes spatially non-uniform, further suppressing the bulk ordering temperature compared to that of the anisotropy-only model.
